question: Does raising the reference-query count n per KV head (n >> top_t) shrink the solved write's |v| toward the teacher's scale, restore total cartridge attention mass toward 0.588, and improve MT — all three together?
variable_under_test: MAX_QUERIES_PER_HEAD (new env knob) in {64, 256, 1024, 4096, 16384} at fixed TOP_T=32; everything else canonical EXP-007-top32 (GRANULARITY=per_layer, SLOT_SELECTION=tfidf, USE_IDF=0, KEY_MODE=freeze, TARGET_MODE=cartridge_plus_doc, RIDGE_LAMBDA=1e-4, RIDGE_SCALE=spectral, DELTA_WEIGHT=1e-2, AM_EXECUTION_MODE=per_document)
baseline_ref: EXP-007-top32 (QA 2.1766157150268555 / MT 2.5483615398406982), reproduced in-process as the n=64 control

numbers.note: top-level numbers are the n=64 CONTROL arm; per-arm numbers below

baseline_reproduced.n64_in_run_eval_vs_EXP-007-top32: EXACT to all 16 printed digits on BOTH splits (2.1766157150268555 / 2.5483615398406982)

value_global_max_abs_vs_n.direction: |v| GROWS monotonically with n (8x from n=64 to n=16384), AWAY from the teacher's scale — the opposite of the B-CASCADE prediction. argmax layer is 34 in every arm.

eval_time_total_cartridge_attention_mass.direction: the 0.588 -> 0.329 routing collapse IS repaired at n >= 1024 and OVERSHOOTS Phase-1 (0.640), with no MT benefit

eval_time_mass_on_S_MT.note: essentially invariant in n; S = per-layer union over the 16 documents of that arm's selected slots

solve_time_ref_mass_on_S_mean_over_36_la.note: computed inside guarded_sparse_am_value_update (value_solve.py) — the standing WORKERS.md requirement; recorded here for the first time in this loop. Cross-checks ORACLE-WRITE's 0.1523 train-time figure.

am_mean_mse_over_16_docs.note: reference-set MSE rises slightly with n, as expected when 32 free rows must fit more constraints; it is also a better-estimated quantity at large n

reference_query_supply_ceiling_per_kv_he.note: The accumulator is NOT the bottleneck. continual.py:172-182 collects every token of every packed reference batch (queries_per_batch='all_tokens', 4 q-heads per KV head), yielding 57344-81920 real reference queries per KV head per document. The historical hard-coded cap of 64 was discarding ~99.9% of them. The paper's 16k-50k regime is fully reachable; n=16384 ran in 201.7 s. No rows were fabricated or padded in any arm.

cost_scaling.note: cost is essentially FLAT in n (spread 154-202 s, within the run-to-run spread of the arms themselves); the per-document teacher-target/prefill work dominates. Raising n by 256x costs 1.23x wall clock. This arm is therefore NOT cost-dominated — it is quality-dominated: it is nearly free and still buys nothing.

diagnostics.mechanism_for_the_v_growth: guarded_sparse_am_value_update (value_solve.py:365-372) stacks the design as [X_new (n x t) ; sqrt(w) I (t x t)] with w=DELTA_WEIGHT=1e-2, i.e. the normal equations are (X_new^T X_new + w I) V_S = X_new^T R_new + w V_S_old. X_new^T X_new grows ~n while the trust-region block stays fixed at t=32 rows, so the relative pull of DELTA_WEIGHT decays like 1/n. RIDGE_LAMBDA is spectral-scaled (lam = 1e-4 * sigma_max(X)^2, itself growing with n) and is therefore scale-invariant and does not compensate. Raising n thus WEAKENS the only magnitude control in the system. Reproduced at unit level on synthetic data with the real function: |v|max 3.523 / 3.826 / 4.237 / 4.642 / 5.801 for n = 64 / 256 / 1024 / 4096 / 16384.

observations: The n=64 control reproduced EXP-007-top32 to all 16 printed digits on both splits in-run (QA 2.1766157150268555 / MT 2.5483615398406982) and reproduced ORACLE-WRITE's standalone control exactly (QA 2.1771795749664307 / MT 2.5524158477783203); the Phase-1 floor control also reproduced exactly (2.23880672454834 / 3.7825491428375244), so the build is default-preserving and every downstream number is on the same ruler. B-CASCADE's joint prediction did not hold, and it failed on the |v| axis in the opposite direction to the one predicted: value_global_max_abs GROWS monotonically with n — 984 (n=64), 1328, 1968, 3344, 7808 (n=16384) — moving 8x further from the teacher's own |63|, with layer 34 the argmax in every arm. The reason is in the solve itself: `guarded_sparse_am_value_update` stacks [X_new (n x t); sqrt(w) I (t x t)], so the normal equations are (X_new^T X_new + w I) V = X_new^T R + w V_old; X_new^T X_new scales with n while the DELTA_WEIGHT trust region stays fixed at 32 rows, so its relative pull decays like 1/n, and the spectral-scaled ridge (lam ~ sigma_max(X)^2, itself growing with n) does not compensate — reproduced at unit level on synthetic data (|v|max 3.52 -> 5.80 across the same sweep). Meanwhile the routing collapse ORACLE-WRITE found IS repaired by more queries and then overshoots: total eval-time cartridge attention mass on MT goes 0.3285 (n=64) / 0.3715 (n=256) / 0.6399 (n=1024) / 0.6395 (n=4096) / 0.6388 (n=16384) against the Phase-1 reference 0.5879, i.e. from -44% to +9% of Phase-1 — and MT did not improve at any n. MT is 2.5524 (control), 2.7716, 2.5744, 2.7114, 2.6943: the best MT in the sweep is the n=64 control, n=1024's +0.022 is deep inside the +-0.1-0.2 noise band ('MT did not move'), and n=256/4096/16384 are +0.219/+0.159/+0.142, i.e. at or outside the band and worse. QA moves the same way (2.1772 control vs 2.2575-2.4097). Eval-time mass_on_S is essentially invariant in n (MT 0.0784-0.0842 vs Phase-1 0.0896), so what n moves is the cartridge's TOTAL share of attention, not the written slots' share of it. The three quantities B-CASCADE bound together are therefore decoupled in the measurement: cartridge routing mass recovered fully (and past Phase-1) while |v| grew and CE did not improve. Solve-time mass_on_S — computed at value_solve.py and never before recorded in this loop — is 0.1585 / 0.1463 / 0.1472 / 0.1451 / 0.1452 averaged over the 36 layers (per-layer range 0.030-0.595 at n=64), cross-checking ORACLE-WRITE's independent 0.1523 train-time figure. am/mean_mse rises slightly with n (0.11906 -> 0.12610), consistent with 32 free rows fitting more constraints. On cost, the sweep is essentially FLAT: phase2 e2e 164.2 / 153.8 / 171.9 / 159.0 / 201.7 s, so a 256x increase in n costs 1.23x wall clock and the per-document prefill/teacher-target work dominates — this is not a cost-dominated point, it is a quality-dominated one. The accumulator ceiling is 57344-81920 real reference queries per KV head per document (continual.py:172-182 keeps every token of every packed batch, 4 q-heads per KV head), so the hard-coded 64 was discarding ~99.9% of the available queries and the AM paper's 16k-50k regime is fully reachable on this box; no rows were fabricated or padded in any arm. Caveats: the eval splits are tiny (QA n=6, MT n=5 batches) so only the n=256 deltas are clearly outside the noise band on both axes; the cartridge-mass series is non-monotone between n=256 (0.3715) and n=1024 (0.6399) — a step change this measurement does not explain; and the sweep varies n at a FIXED DELTA_WEIGHT=1e-2, so it cannot separate 'more queries do not help' from 'more queries help but the 1/n decay of the trust region cancels it', which would need DELTA_WEIGHT scaled with n. This sits alongside DIAG-OBJ-c, which drove the same trust-region axis to its endpoint (DELTA_WEIGHT=0 -> |v| 21504, both losses +13).
